metadata.title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
metadata.abstract: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. metadata.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
metadata.abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.

metadata.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
metadata.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|\Omega|<\infty$, and let $u_\Omega$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $\Delta u_\Omega=\chi_\Omega$. We prove the sharp inequality \[ \int_\Omega|\nabla u_\Omega|^2\,\mathrm{d} x \leq\frac{1}{2N\omega_{N-1}} \iint_{\Omega\times\Omega}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $\omega_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $\Omega$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.

metadata.title: Fisher Geometry of Circular Wrapped Normals: Completion and Curvature
metadata.abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher geometry of the two-parameter circular wrapped normal family. Although its finite parameters form a cylinder, its metric completion is a disk: adjoining the uniform law extends the Fisher metric to a positive-definite real-analytic metric. The Gaussian curvature vanishes at the added point, is positive nearby, and tends to $-1/2$ as the underlying standard deviation tends to zero. We prove that the curvature has exactly one nonuniform zero radius and exactly one critical radius, the latter a nondegenerate positive maximum. Opposite points sufficiently close to uniformity are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic through the uniform law, so their intrinsic distance is not attained inside the nonuniform family. In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. Wrapping strictly decreases Fisher information in every nonzero tangent direction, while the information deficit and its fixed-order derivatives are exponentially small as the standard deviation tends to zero. The curvature theorem is proved by convergent series and explicit analytic remainder estimates; numerical figures serve only as illustrations.

In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. metadata.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
metadata.abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact Kähler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-Kähler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.

metadata.title: Maximum Diversity and Support Transitions on Disks and Three-Dimensional Balls
metadata.abstract: For the similarity kernel $e^{-|x-y|}$, we determine the probability measure of maximum diversity on every planar disk and three-dimensional ball, answering a question of Leinster and Roff. In each dimension the measure is uniform on the boundary up to a threshold. Above it, the support is a closed central ball and the outer sphere, separated by a mass-free annulus. In dimensions two and three, their conjecture of finitely many supporting spheres therefore holds only up to the respective threshold. We obtain the measure explicitly up to one scalar root in three dimensions and through Fredholm integral equations and a scalar contact equation in the plane. Computations in dimensions four and five suggest that interior supporting spheres appear one at a time.

metadata.title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
metadata.abstract: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

metadata.title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.

metadata.title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.

metadata.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
metadata.abstract: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

metadata.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
metadata.abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting Kähler-Ricci solitons. metadata.title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
metadata.abstract: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

metadata.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
metadata.abstract: Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

metadata.title: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients
metadata.abstract: Let $M_n=(\mathrm{PU}(2)^n\rtimes S_n)\backslash\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$ be the space of projective $n$-qubit unitaries modulo local unitaries and permutations of the qubits. We prove that for all sufficiently large $n$ the manifold $M_n$ carries exactly two $\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. Both Einstein metrics have uniformly bounded diameter after normalizing two-qubit costs, although approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates. In contrast, we construct non-Einstein metrics with nonnegative Ricci curvature and exponentially growing typical control distances, and determine the sharp curvature threshold for this family.

metadata.title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
metadata.abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

metadata.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
metadata.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

metadata.title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $\mu$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work ( arXiv:2008.07093 ), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincaré inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

metadata.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
metadata.abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.

metadata.title: New explicit examples of Mannheim pair in $\mathbb{L}^3$
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit examples of Mannheim pairs, in the classical sense, in Minkowski 3-space $\mathbb{L}^3$, one for each of the five types of such pairs. In our main examples the Mannheim curve is neither a helix nor a slant helix. For each example we give the complete Frenet apparatus of both curves of the pair and their Cartesian coordinates in terms of elementary functions. The construction writes the tangent indicatrix in angular coordinates and uses a suitable auxiliary angle function, which reduces all the relevant integrals to elementary form; it is carried out both starting from the Mannheim curve and starting from its partner. In these coordinates, we also characterize the helices and the slant helices with timelike axis. We also prove, for the five types, that a Mannheim curve is a slant helix if and only if its partner is a helix, and we give an explicit example of such a pair.

metadata.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
metadata.abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.

metadata.title: Solitons on Statistical Manifolds and Their Submanifolds
metadata.abstract:
Statistical manifolds, introduced by Amari in information geometry, carry a pair of dual torsion-free connections $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ together with a Riemannian metric. In this chapter we survey the theory of \emph{statistical solitons}, that is, vector fields and constants that solve the Ricci-soliton equation simultaneously for $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$, together with the statistical analogue of almost quasi-Yamabe solitons. We discuss two principal settings: (i) statistical warped products $\R	imes_f N_2$ and $N_1	imes_f\R$ for (pseudo) Riemannian manifolds $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$, where the soliton equation constrains the warping function; and (ii) statistical submanifolds of Kenmotsu statistical manifolds, where the position of the Reeb field $\xi$ relative to the submanifold and the presence of concircular or concurrent vector fields determine the Einstein, $\eta$-Einstein or quasi-Einstein character of the submanifold. We further review the results of Blaga and Chen on gradient solitons and statistical structures, in particular the connections $
abla^{	heta}$ defined by a $1$-form, volume formulas and bounds for the Ricci tensor. We also describe Chen-type inequalities for statistical warped product submanifolds, which give the extrinsic context in which such solitons live. Key steps of the proofs, remarks on the sharpness of hypotheses, worked examples, and open problems are included.

metadata.title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
metadata.abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

metadata.title: The geometry of Floquet states
metadata.abstract: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

metadata.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
metadata.abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

metadata.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
metadata.abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_\mu$ and the mass element $q_\sigma$. We show that $p_\mu-q_\sigma=wp_\mu$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

metadata.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
metadata.abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

analysisBasis.abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

metadata.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
metadata.abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

metadata.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
metadata.abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

metadata.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
metadata.abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichmüller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.

analysisBasis.abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichmüller spaces. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.

metadata.title: On $κ$-covering minima
metadata.abstract: We introduce $\kappa$-covering minima by requiring the permutation simplices of one independent lattice frame to fit into translates of a common dilate of a convex body. We prove a lower bound for their normalized product, with coefficient $(n+1)/2^n$ for centrally symmetric bodies and an explicit dependence on Minkowski asymmetry in general. On Euclidean balls, the supremum over full-rank lattices of the ratio of the resulting fitting radius to the covering radius has order $\sqrt n$. We also establish basic comparisons with classical lattice minima and bounds under products, projections, Minkowski addition, and free direct sums. We extend the definition by allowing projected periodic lattice triangulations. These extended minima agree with the classical covering minima on ellipsoids.

metadata.title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
metadata.abstract: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.

metadata.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
metadata.abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.

metadata.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
metadata.abstract: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{\lambda_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{\lambda_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.

metadata.title: Dually flat structure of von Mises-Fisher distributions
metadata.abstract: The von Mises--Fisher (vMF) distribution is the natural exponential family analogue of the normal distribution on the unit hypersphere. metadata.title: Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Ampère equations II: Hermitian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Ampère masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Ampère mass in the Hermitian setting.

metadata.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
metadata.abstract: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

analysisBasis.abstract: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

metadata.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
metadata.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

metadata.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
metadata.abstract: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (\Delta u)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.

metadata.title: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension
metadata.abstract: In this work, we formalize the concept of intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes introduced in Li et al. (2018), which measures the structural complexity of learning problems by training along randomly generated subspaces. We define the intrinsic dimension of a set $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ as the minimal dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ such that a random plane of dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ in $\mathbb{R}^p$ intersects $\Theta$ with probability one. We show that it is a generalized notion of co-dimension that depends on the global geometry of $\Theta$. We study mathematical properties of the intrinsic dimension and develop techniques to estimate the intrinsic dimension of sets $\Theta$ that arise in learning problems. More specifically, we derive upper and/or lower bounds where $\Theta$ is the set of optimal parameters in student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks, including finite and infinite sample cases, and with and without regularization. We discuss how our theory leads to novel types of generalization bounds, thereby showing that the intrinsic dimension is a measure of learning complexity. Our results connect techniques from seemingly different areas of machine learning research such as classification of symmetries of ReLU networks and stochastic geometry.

metadata.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
metadata.abstract: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vignéras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

metadata.title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
metadata.abstract: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

analysisBasis.abstract: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

metadata.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
metadata.abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.

metadata.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
metadata.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. metadata.title: Three-dimensional noncompact trans-Sasakian $η$-Einstein manifolds
metadata.abstract: We classify connected, simply connected, noncompact three-dimensional trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds. In [1], we showed that, in the compact case, such a manifold is either of $\beta$-Kenmotsu type or homothetic to a Sasakian manifold. In this paper, in the noncompact case, we find families of trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds that are neither $\beta$-Kenmotsu nor homothetic to Sasakian manifolds. These families have infinitely many degrees of freedom. We give these nontrivial metrics explicitly. We also give a structure theorem for the case in which the characteristic vector field is Palais-nonregular.

metadata.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
metadata.abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

metadata.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
metadata.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

analysisBasis.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. metadata.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
metadata.abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

metadata.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
metadata.abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

metadata.title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(α,β)$-Metrics
metadata.abstract: Let $F=\alpha\Phi(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-metric, where $q=\|\beta\|_\alpha^2$ and $s=\beta/\alpha$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $\alpha$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.

metadata.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
metadata.abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth Möbius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

metadata.title: Whitham Deformations of Nodal Spectral Curves of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
metadata.abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. Deformations that preserve the periods, called Whitham deformations, are well understood for nonsingular curves, where the isoperiodic sets are manifolds. We extend Whitham deformations to curves with ordinary double points that are fixed by the real involution. At such curves the isoperiodic sets remain manifolds and are transverse to the curves with double points, so Whitham deformations can change the genus of the spectral curve. We describe how the double points open, and when the derivative of the normalized Willmore energy vanishes at a nodal curve. By inserting double points, we show that every value of a discrete invariant of the isoperiodic sets found in previous work occurs.

metadata.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
metadata.abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Schütz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

metadata.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
metadata.abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

metadata.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
metadata.abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) on the classification of pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal to each other under the appropriate pullback. The proof is based on a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. The compatible graphs are used on the open dense set where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations are identities between smooth tensors, so they extend by continuity across the points where the tuple jumps. Consequently, our classification holds without any assumption of local constancy of the characteristic tuple.

metadata.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $λ$-convex bodies
metadata.abstract: For a given $\lambda > 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/\lambda$. We show that among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $\lambda$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/\lambda$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $\lambda > 0$.

metadata.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
metadata.abstract: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.

metadata.title: Johnson optimality and uniqueness for distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$
metadata.abstract: We prove that a two-distance set in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$ has at most $d(d+1)/2$ points for every $d\ge9$. Equality in full affine dimension characterizes the Johnson construction; for $d\ge10$, the full-dimensional condition is automatic. The proof separates configurations according to the connectivity of the short-distance graph. The connected case uses root lattices and intersection theorems, while the disconnected case uses an orthogonal decomposition into component direction spaces and the span of their center differences. We also prove a relative bound for Euclidean two-distance sets and show that equality forces sphericity. Together with the Larman--Rogers--Seidel theorem, these results give maximum cardinality $d(d+1)/2$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $275$ for $d=22$, without exhaustive enumeration.

metadata.title: Localization in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
metadata.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity provides holographic access to strongly coupled six-dimensional superconformal theories through its highest-dimensional supersymmetric AdS vacua. Its unique spinor-bilinear geometry and massive higher-form dynamics make systematic analysis and solution-finding distinctively challenging. Relative equivariant localization can obtain supersymmetric observables in odd dimensions from fixed-point data on an auxiliary even-dimensional filling, without an explicit solution. We extend this approach to seven dimensions in maximal Cartan-gauged supergravity with all gauge fields active. We formulate the Euclidean action and Killing-spinor equations in terms of field strengths, and construct a bilinear system adapted to the change in spinor reality conditions from symplectic-Majorana to Majorana. On the non-null gauged active spinor branch, independent, oppositely R-charged spinors are paired by Majorana conjugation on the same complex background. One algebraic gauging correction and two algebraic bilinear projections suffice to extend the equal-charge sector to independent Cartan charges, and the underlying efficient reorganization also applies in the Lorentzian theory. Massive 3-form self-duality fixes the quartic anomaly class and determines the higher-form fixed-point datum from Abelian moment maps. Localization at the single fixed point of the filling recovers the general supersymmetric AdS$_7$ black-hole action, without extending the solution. We prove gauge-covariant Killing-spinor invariance under the combined supersymmetric Killing flow and R-symmetry action, deriving the linear chemical-potential constraint. Extremizing the constrained entropy functional and requiring real positive stationary entropy yields the nonlinear charge relation within the Euclidean analysis, equivalent to Lorentzian horizon extremality for the known spherical black-hole family.

metadata.title: Willmore inequalities beyond the injectivity radius
metadata.abstract: We generalize a method first introduced by Li, Yau, Simon, and Topping (for closed surfaces immersed in the flat Euclidean space), and we establish a global-in-nature estimate, with an explicit cut-locus contribution, on the Willmore energy of closed surfaces that are immersed in a complete Riemannian three-manifold and need not be embedded. Our estimate applies to ambient spaces whose sectional curvature is bounded above and whose injectivity radius may be finite. For positive upper curvature bounds, the global weighted estimates require an explicit radius restriction. The Willmore energy is bounded below by a functional involving the self-intersection number of the surface and the injectivity radius of the ambient space. Furthermore, by investigating in what sense our inequalities are optimal and realized by geodesic spheres in constant curvature spaces, we are led to introduce a weighted version of the Willmore functional, which is adapted to geodesic spheres in the model spaces and takes the sectional curvature of the ambient space into account. As a corollary, we obtain sufficient conditions for an immersed surface in a curved space to be embedded.

metadata.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
metadata.abstract: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

metadata.title: Almost Homogeneity Characterizes Almost Bi-Lipschitz Euclidean Embeddability
metadata.abstract: A metric space admits an almost bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Euclidean space if and only if it is almost homogeneous. We prove the sufficient direction, complementing the known necessary condition. More quantitatively, we bound the target dimension and the embedding constants for every logarithmic exponent $\gamma>1$. The bounds depend only on the covering parameters in the almost homogeneity condition. In particular every doubling metric space admits such an embedding. This answers a question of Margaris and Robinson and the almost bi-Lipschitz part of a question of Olson and Robinson. As a consequence, the difference set of the image is doubling, which answers the difference-set questions of Olson and Robinson and of Margaris.

metadata.title: Some remarks on robust features of surfaces in 4-space
metadata.abstract: We study robust features of smooth surfaces in 4-space associated with contact with lines and hyperplanes. We investigate the local and multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and height functions that describe these contacts and their corresponding geometric loci on the surface. At an $A_4$-singularity of a height function, we show that the $A_3$-curve and the $A_1A_2$-curve are generically tangent with contact of order $2$. We further establish criteria for the versality of the families of height functions and orthogonal projections in terms of the regularity of the $B_2$-curve and $S_2$-curve, respectively. Finally, we obtain the $[A_2]$- and $(A_0S_0)_2$-curves arising from multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and describe their tangency properties at the $B_3$- and $H_3$-singularities.

metadata.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
metadata.abstract: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

analysisBasis.abstract: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
